theme: The marriage supper; the rider; the thousand years; final judgment
readingInstruction: Read Revelation 19:1-20:15. This is a long and important reading, covering the marriage supper of the Lamb, the rider on the white horse, the binding of Satan, the thousand years, and the great white throne. Read slowly, and notice how each scene answers the question of who wins.
settingTheScene: After the fall of Babylon, heaven erupts in praise, and the book moves to the return of Christ, the final defeat of evil, and the last judgment. Chapter 20 contains the only mention of the “thousand years” in the Bible, and Christians have understood it in three major ways. The book’s purpose is not to settle a timetable but to assure the church that the Lamb wins and that evil is finally and fully destroyed.
observation: “Hallelujah! For the Lord our God the Almighty reigns” (19:6).
“The marriage of the Lamb has come, and his Bride has made herself ready” (19:7).
“Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb” (19:9).
“A white horse! The one sitting on it is called Faithful and True” (19:11).
“King of kings and Lord of lords” (19:16).
“And bound him for a thousand years” (20:2).
“Blessed and holy is the one who shares in the first resurrection!” (20:6).
“And if anyone’s name was not found written in the book of life, he was thrown into the lake of fire” (20:15).
interpretation:
A great multitude in heaven cries out, “Hallelujah! Salvation and glory and power belong to our God, for his judgments are true and just; for he has judged the great prostitute.” These are the only “Hallelujahs” in the New Testament. The twenty-four elders and four living creatures say “Amen,” and a voice from the throne calls all God’s servants to praise. Then the multitude, “like the roar of many waters and like the sound of mighty peals of thunder,” cries, “Hallelujah! For the Lord our God the Almighty reigns. Let us rejoice and exult and give him the glory, for the marriage of the Lamb has come, and his Bride has made herself ready; it was granted her to clothe herself with fine linen, bright and pure,” which is “the righteous deeds of the saints.” This is a contrast with the prostitute. The Bride is the church. “Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb.” John falls down to worship the angel, but is told, “You must not do that! I am a fellow servant… Worship God. For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.”

Then heaven opens: “a white horse! The one sitting on it is called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he judges and makes war.” His eyes are like a flame of fire, on his head are many diadems, he wears a robe dipped in blood, and his name is “The Word of God.” The armies of heaven follow him on white horses, clothed in fine linen. “From his mouth comes a sharp sword with which to strike down the nations.” Note that the weapon is his word. On his robe and thigh is written the name “King of kings and Lord of lords.” An angel invites the birds to the great supper of God. The beast and the kings gather to make war against him, but the beast and the false prophet are captured and thrown alive into the lake of fire, and the rest are killed by the sword from his mouth. No battle is actually described: the Word speaks and it is done.

In chapter 20, an angel with the key of the bottomless pit seizes “the dragon, that ancient serpent, who is the devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years, and threw him into the pit, and shut it and sealed it over him, so that he might not deceive the nations any longer.” Then John sees thrones with those given authority to judge, and the souls of those beheaded for the testimony of Jesus, who “came to life and reigned with Christ for a thousand years.” This is called the first resurrection. “Blessed and holy is the one who shares in the first resurrection! Over such the second death has no power.” After the thousand years, Satan is released for a short time, deceives the nations (Gog and Magog), and surrounds the camp of the saints, but fire comes down from heaven and consumes them, and the devil is thrown into the lake of fire.

Christians have three main views on the millennium. Premillennialists believe Christ returns before a literal thousand-year reign on earth: historic premillennialists hold that the church will go through the tribulation, and dispensational premillennialists hold that the church is raptured before it. Amillennialists believe the thousand years is symbolic of the present age between Christ’s first and second comings, in which Satan is bound in the sense that he cannot prevent the gospel from reaching the nations, and the saints who have died reign with Christ in heaven. Postmillennialists believe that the gospel will bring a golden age before Christ returns. Faithful Christians hold each of these views. The points on which all agree are that Christ will return visibly, there will be a resurrection and judgment, and the final state is the new creation.

The chapter ends with the great white throne, which we examine on Day 892: the dead, great and small, stand before the throne, books are opened, and death and Hades are thrown into the lake of fire. The last enemy is destroyed.
connection: Psalm 2 and 110 are the background of the rider’s rule with the rod of iron. Isaiah 63:1-6 describes the one whose garments are stained. Ephesians 5:25-32 and 2 Corinthians 11:2 describe the church as the Bride. Isaiah 25:6-9 describes a feast on the mountain. Matthew 22:1-14 and 25:1-13 are parables of the wedding. 2 Thessalonians 2:8 says Christ will destroy the lawless one by the breath of his mouth. Ezekiel 38-39 describes Gog and Magog. John 5:28-29 and 1 Corinthians 15:20-28 speak of resurrection and the last enemy. Colossians 2:15 and Matthew 12:29 speak of binding the strong man.
application:
Praise God today with the word “Hallelujah,” and think about what it means: “praise the LORD.”

Think of the marriage supper of the Lamb as your future. Ask how it changes what you live for now.

When Christians disagree on the millennium, practice charity. Which parts do all agree on, and how can you focus on them?
prayerPrompts: Thank him for inviting you to the marriage supper of the Lamb.
Ask him to keep you faithful to the end.
